summary:
I've been picking up SwarmUI where I left off and mostly working on TheLongRest, the D&D campaign app I built and run for my own table.

The bigger recent chunk was Adventure Import: paste in an adventure you already own, and it derives NPCs, monster stats, and session beats from the text instead of storing the source material. That last part matters — I never keep the published prose, only what a DM actually reviews and approves, because the content-safety rule I set for myself is "keep mechanics, drop prose." I used it to prep a real one-shot from a physical book I own, and along the way found the model was inventing full stat blocks from memory for monsters it only had passing references to, so I added a grounding pass that demotes anything not actually in the source text to a stub instead of a hallucination.

Alongside that I added a proper feedback page for playtests — bug log, a versioned survey, DM-only results — with real anonymity: choosing "don't attach my name" means no user id is stored at all, enforced by a separate receipt table that tracks "already answered" without ever linking back to the response. I also tracked down a nasty realtime bug where dice rolls and presence would silently die the moment anyone closed a side panel; turned out the app was creating multiple listeners on what should've been one shared channel per campaign, and closing any of them tore down the channel for everyone else on the page too.

On the infrastructure side, I finally sat down and looked at four months of power-draw data I'd been logging on my home GPU box and never actually read — turned out the number matched my back-of-envelope estimate, so I built a small dashboard for it instead of trusting a static report. I also chased down a screen-eviction bug across my model-serving setup that was costing minutes on the first request of the day; the model was getting evicted from GPU memory between uses and forced to reprocess its entire context from scratch, fixed with a save/restore of that state plus a periodic keep-warm job.

highlights.oneLiner: Back on SwarmUI, the front-end that drives local ComfyUI image generation.
Fixed model-eviction stalls with KV save/restore plus a periodic keep-warm job.
